# One noncentral section coordinate does not guarantee positive capacity curvature

This is an exact obstruction to a proposed row-level lemma, not to stochastic containment or OC. In particular no maximizing stochastic completion is claimed.

Let a tetrahedral cap have raw vertex margins c=(1,5,-5,-8). For positive p,q,r,s its cap fraction is

    P(p,q,-r,-s)
      =[p^3/((p+r)(p+s))-q^3/((q+r)(q+s))]/(p-q).

The apparent repeated-height singularity cancels. At the indicated margins, write g=grad_c P and H=Hess_c P. Exact differentiation gives

    P=331/1404,   f_V(0)=(sum g_j)/3=61/1404,
    b=g/(3 f_V(0))
      =(1171/3294,1561/4758,98/549,2953/21411).

Only b_0 exceeds 1/3: b_0-1/3=73/3294 and 1/3-b_1=25/4758, while both excluded coordinates are also below 1/3. Thus the captured pair has exactly one noncentral coordinate.

The strictly positive row

    x=(270,26,636,819)/900

has a unique proper minimizing threshold t=331/900. Indeed t1-x=(61/900)c and scale invariance of P gives t F_x'(t)=3P exactly from P/f_V(0)=331/61. Concavity of F_x^(1/3) makes this stationary threshold globally minimizing; positive-row uniqueness applies. Every entry of x is strictly between zero and one.

Take tangent directions

    v=(g_1,-g_0,0,0),  w=(0,0,g_3,-g_2).

They lie in g-perpendicular. The matrix of the cap Hessian on their span is exactly

    Q_11=298246999/303084016455168,
    Q_12=114611287/454626024682752,
    Q_22=1004887915/681939037024128,
    det Q=23880754822693393/17223735193236852561853857792>0.

Thus Q is positive definite. The three vectors v,w,c form a basis of g-perpendicular: the first two are independent within the positive and negative coordinate pairs; expressing c as their sum would require the sum of its g-weighted positive entries to vanish, which is impossible. Homogeneity gives Hc=-g, so c is the null direction of H restricted to g-perpendicular and has zero cross terms there.

The fully optimized capacity Hessian is negative semidefinite, with only its radial kernel. To see this without dropping threshold motion, decompose any direction as v0+l1 with g dot v0=0. The Schur-completed formula is

    (v0+l1)^T Hess(phi)(v0+l1)
      =-K[v0^T H v0+(eta dot v0-l dP)^2/B],

where K>0, B>0 and eta=H1. Both terms are nonnegative here. Equality forces v0 proportional to c and l=-that proportionality constant, hence gives the radial direction c-1=-x after normalization. Scaling back preserves the inertia.

Consequently the unresolved two-full-row/one-zero-row configuration cannot be dismissed by asserting that a cap with only one noncentral captured coordinate must have positive optimized curvature. The full maximizing equations remain additional information.

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/certify_single_noncentral_tetrahedral_minimum_root.py` computes the exact fractions and asserts all the stated signs. Its role is to verify these explicit identities; the mathematical certificate is displayed above.
